claims.claim: Across a 3,000-op randomized pressure run with three concurrent readers holding pins (1,906 pinned reads, 916 total evictions), zero pinned entries were evicted: the pin table protects every entry a running unit holds.

Mutation control: with pinning disabled (pin table ignored in the evict path), the same seeded rig produces 12 evictions of pinned entries while the pinned baseline on the identical seed stays clean - the detector fires on the broken state and is silent on the good one.

negative_controls.description: pinning_enabled=False evicts entries whose pin count is raised; the violation hook records the actual eviction (not the attempt), so the pinned baseline records nothing.
negative_controls.good_state_output: baseline violations=0 across 443 evictions with pins live

implementation.pinning: acquire() raises a per-key pin count; release() drops it; LRU prune skips pinned entries (reference-count style)
implementation.violation_semantics: recorded only when a pinned entry is ACTUALLY evicted (mutant path), never on a protected attempt
implementation.production_note: platform/plugin/cache.py Cache.prune evicts strictly by mtime LRU and has no pin concept; the pinned reference implementation is the measured layer per the unit contract

signals.a: eviction log cross-referenced against the pin table at eviction time
signals.b: pinned readers' read outcomes recorded during the pressure run (1,906 reads)

residual_unknowns.claim: Production Cache.prune has no pin/reference-count concept, so the pinned property cannot be bound to it today; if production gains pinning, re-bind these probes to Cache.prune and retire the probe-local implementation.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Re-bind probe1/probe2 to the production prune once a pin API exists; keep the pinning-disabled mutant as the detector control.
